Mitigation stated: all SGL units are certified for ISO 45001, top management is committed to a 'Zero Incident, safe work culture' through the Safety Health & Environment Policy, and an online digital platform has been introduced for real-time reporting and monitoring. risks.note: Named a RISK with negative financial implications in the BRSR materiality table. The Company describes a regulatory intelligence programme and advanced digital online tools to monitor adherence, and states that 'achieving zero regulatory non-compliance is a relentless pursuit'. The contingent-liability note corroborates live exposure - a disputed excise duty on inter-unit transfer of machinery pending before the Jurisdiction Officer after an Appellate Tribunal order, and a penalty proceeding under Section 122(2)(b) of the CGST Act, 2017 read with Section 74.

Both Waste Management and Water and Wastewater Management are flagged as RISKS with negative financial implications. Mitigations disclosed: all units certified to ISO 14001, hazardous and non-hazardous waste segregated and disposed per applicable norms, all units equipped with wastewater treatment facilities and rainwater harvesting. Tightening norms or a lapse at a site is a structural cost and licence-to-operate risk for an India-only manufacturing footprint.

This feeds both input costs and the capex cycles of the customer industries the Company serves.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and energy-price shock in the macro environment
risks.note: The Board's Report describes a global economy 'heavily impacted by geopolitical instability, structural shifts, and sticky inflation' with divergence 'due to a massive Energy supply shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East', and states that per the IMF 'potential escalations in West Asian conflicts and volatile crude prices remain primary risk factors'. This feeds both input costs and the capex cycles of the customer industries the Company serves.

The BRSR discloses that one activity - design and manufacture of gears, gear boxes, geared motors and gear assemblies plus refurbishing and repairing of gear boxes - accounts for 100% of turnover, and that operations are National only, with three plants and one office and Nil international plants or offices. There is no product-line or manufacturing-location diversification to absorb a downturn in the industrial gear cycle.

The Board's Report records that Mr. Ranjan Kumar Pati, Chief Financial Officer, resigned with effect from 19th March 2026, leaving a KMP position open at the balance-sheet date; the other KMP named are the CEO & Whole-time Director and the Company Secretary & Compliance Officer. Reported as the AR states it - the AR does not itself characterise this as a risk.
